# p5.geo API reference

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs` from docs/templates/api.hbs and the JSDoc comments in src/. Edit those, not this file. -->

p5.geo targets p5.js 2.x. Coordinates are always **latitude, longitude**, in that order.

- [createGeoMap()](#createGeoMap)
- [GeoMap](#GeoMap)
- [geoPoints()](#geoPoints), [geoLines()](#geoLines), [geoPolygons()](#geoPolygons)
- [p5.geo](#geo)
- [LatLon](#LatLon), [View](#View)
- [Passing numbers and strings](#passing-numbers-and-strings)

<a name="createGeoMap"></a>

## createGeoMap([options]) ⇒ <code>GeoMap</code>
Creates a map behind the canvas. Call it after `createCanvas()`.

The canvas stays on top, transparent and click-through: the map handles dragging and
scrolling, and `mouseX`, `mouseY` and p5's mouse events keep working. Call `clear()`
(not `background()`) at the start of `draw()` so the map stays visible.

MapLibre GL JS is loaded automatically from jsDelivr, and attribution for the map data
is shown automatically. The map can't be rotated or tilted, because shapes drawn on the
canvas couldn't follow.

**Kind**: global function  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [options] | <code>Object</code> |  |  |
| [options.center] | <code>Array.&lt;number&gt;</code> \| [<code>LatLon</code>](#LatLon) | <code>[0, 0]</code> | Where the map is centered, as   `[lat, lon]` or `{ lat, lon }` (`{ lat, lng }` also works). |
| [options.zoom] | <code>number</code> | <code>2</code> | Zoom level. See [zoom](#GeoMap+zoom). |
| [options.basemap] | <code>string</code> \| <code>Object</code> \| <code>false</code> | <code>&quot;&#x27;positron&#x27;&quot;</code> | `'positron'`, `'liberty'` or   `'bright'` (keyless [OpenFreeMap](https://openfreemap.org/) styles), a MapLibre style URL   or style object, or `false` for no map: then nothing is added to the page and the   `GeoMap` only converts coordinates. |
| [options.interactive] | <code>boolean</code> | <code>true</code> | Whether the map can be dragged and zoomed.   With `false`, it stays where the sketch puts it. See [interactive](#GeoMap+interactive). |
| [options.mapOptions] | <code>Object</code> |  | Extra options for   [maplibregl.Map](https://maplibre.org/maplibre-gl-js/docs/API/type-aliases/MapOptions/). |
| [options.maplibregl] | <code>Object</code> |  | A MapLibre GL JS namespace to use instead of   loading one. A global `maplibregl` is also used if present. |

**Example**  
```js
let myMap;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(800, 600);
  myMap = createGeoMap({ center: [35.68, 139.76], zoom: 12 });
}

function draw() {
  clear();
  const p = myMap.toScreen(35.6586, 139.7454); // Tokyo Tower
  circle(p.x, p.y, 20);
}
```

<a name="GeoMap"></a>

## GeoMap
The geographic view of a sketch: where the map is centered, how far it is zoomed,
and how latitude/longitude map onto the canvas. Create one with [createGeoMap](#createGeoMap).

With a basemap (the default), MapLibre draws the map behind the p5 canvas and handles
dragging and scrolling; the canvas stays transparent and click-through.
With `basemap: false`, it only converts coordinates, with no map and no changes to the page.

Methods accept numeric strings as well as numbers (see
[Passing numbers and strings](#passing-numbers-and-strings)).

**Kind**: global class  

* [GeoMap](#GeoMap)
    * [.ready](#GeoMap+ready) : [<code>Promise.&lt;GeoMap&gt;</code>](#GeoMap)
    * [.maplibre](#GeoMap+maplibre) : <code>Object</code>
    * [.toScreen(lat, [lon])](#GeoMap+toScreen) ⇒ <code>p5.Vector</code> \| <code>Array.&lt;p5.Vector&gt;</code>
    * [.fromScreen(x, y)](#GeoMap+fromScreen) ⇒ [<code>LatLon</code>](#LatLon)
    * [.contains(polygon, x, y)](#GeoMap+contains) ⇒ <code>boolean</code>
    * [.isMouseOver(polygon)](#GeoMap+isMouseOver) ⇒ <code>boolean</code>
    * [.center([lat], [lon])](#GeoMap+center) ⇒ [<code>LatLon</code>](#LatLon) \| [<code>GeoMap</code>](#GeoMap)
    * [.zoom([level])](#GeoMap+zoom) ⇒ <code>number</code> \| [<code>GeoMap</code>](#GeoMap)
    * [.interactive([enabled])](#GeoMap+interactive) ⇒ <code>boolean</code> \| [<code>GeoMap</code>](#GeoMap)
    * [.fit(data, [options])](#GeoMap+fit) ⇒ [<code>GeoMap</code>](#GeoMap)
    * [.flyTo(lat, lon, [zoom])](#GeoMap+flyTo) ⇒ [<code>GeoMap</code>](#GeoMap)
    * [.remove()](#GeoMap+remove)

<a name="GeoMap+ready"></a>

### myMap.ready : <code>Promise.&lt;GeoMap&gt;</code>
Resolves to the `GeoMap` once the basemap has been created, or right away with
`basemap: false`. There's no need to wait for it to draw: `toScreen()` works from the start.

**Kind**: instance property of [<code>GeoMap</code>](#GeoMap)  
<a name="GeoMap+maplibre"></a>

### myMap.maplibre : <code>Object</code>
The underlying [maplibregl.Map](https://maplibre.org/maplibre-gl-js/docs/API/classes/Map/),
for anything p5.geo doesn't cover. `null` until [ready](#GeoMap+ready) resolves, and always
`null` with `basemap: false`.

**Kind**: instance property of [<code>GeoMap</code>](#GeoMap)  
<a name="GeoMap+toScreen"></a>

### myMap.toScreen(lat, [lon]) ⇒ <code>p5.Vector</code> \| <code>Array.&lt;p5.Vector&gt;</code>
Converts a latitude and longitude to a position on the canvas.

Also accepts `{ lat, lon }` or `[lat, lon]`, or an array of them, which returns an array
of vectors. Use the array form for lines and polygon outlines, such as the `path`,
`outer` and `holes` from [geoLines](#geoLines) and [geoPolygons](#geoPolygons).

The basemap repeats the world sideways, so a single point goes on the copy of the world
nearest the center of the canvas. An array is moved as one piece, so shapes never tear
apart across the antimeridian. Works before the basemap has loaded.

Positions are measured from the top-left corner, like `mouseX` and `mouseY`. On a `WEBGL`
canvas, where (0, 0) is the center, call `translate(-width / 2, -height / 2)` before drawing.

**Kind**: instance method of [<code>GeoMap</code>](#GeoMap)  
**Returns**: <code>p5.Vector</code> \| <code>Array.&lt;p5.Vector&gt;</code> - The position on the canvas, or one per point.  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lat | <code>number</code> \| [<code>LatLon</code>](#LatLon) \| <code>Array.&lt;number&gt;</code> \| [<code>Array.&lt;LatLon&gt;</code>](#LatLon) | Latitude, or a point, or an array of points. |
| [lon] | <code>number</code> | Longitude, when `lat` is a number. |

**Example**  
```js
const p = myMap.toScreen(35.6586, 139.7454);
circle(p.x, p.y, 20);
```
**Example**  
```js
beginShape();
for (const p of myMap.toScreen(country.outer)) vertex(p.x, p.y);
endShape(CLOSE);
```
<a name="GeoMap+fromScreen"></a>

### myMap.fromScreen(x, y) ⇒ <code>LatLon</code>
Converts a position on the canvas to a latitude and longitude.

**Kind**: instance method of [<code>GeoMap</code>](#GeoMap)  

| Param | Type |
| --- | --- |
| x | <code>number</code> | 
| y | <code>number</code> | 

**Example**  
```js
const here = myMap.fromScreen(mouseX, mouseY);
text(`${here.lat.toFixed(4)}, ${here.lon.toFixed(4)}`, mouseX, mouseY);
```
<a name="GeoMap+contains"></a>

### myMap.contains(polygon, x, y) ⇒ <code>boolean</code>
Whether a position on the canvas is inside a polygon, as drawn with `toScreen()`: inside
its outline and outside every hole. For the mouse, use [isMouseOver](#GeoMap+isMouseOver).

**Kind**: instance method of [<code>GeoMap</code>](#GeoMap)  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| polygon | <code>Object</code> \| [<code>Array.&lt;LatLon&gt;</code>](#LatLon) | An item   from [geoPolygons](#geoPolygons), or an outline as an array of `{ lat, lon }`. |
| x | <code>number</code> |  |
| y | <code>number</code> |  |

**Example**  
```js
const touched = countries.filter((c) => myMap.contains(c, touches[0].x, touches[0].y));
```
<a name="GeoMap+isMouseOver"></a>

### myMap.isMouseOver(polygon) ⇒ <code>boolean</code>
Whether the mouse is over a polygon, as drawn with `toScreen()`. Always `false` while the
mouse is outside the canvas.

**Kind**: instance method of [<code>GeoMap</code>](#GeoMap)  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| polygon | <code>Object</code> \| [<code>Array.&lt;LatLon&gt;</code>](#LatLon) | An item   from [geoPolygons](#geoPolygons), or an outline as an array of `{ lat, lon }`. |

**Example**  
```js
for (const country of countries) {
  fill(myMap.isMouseOver(country) ? 'tomato' : 'white');
  beginShape();
  for (const p of myMap.toScreen(country.outer)) vertex(p.x, p.y);
  endShape(CLOSE);
}
```
<a name="GeoMap+center"></a>

### myMap.center([lat], [lon]) ⇒ <code>LatLon</code> \| <code>GeoMap</code>
Gets or sets the center of the map. With no arguments, returns the center.
With `center(lat, lon)`, `center([lat, lon])` or `center({ lat, lon })`, moves the map there.

**Kind**: instance method of [<code>GeoMap</code>](#GeoMap)  
**Returns**: [<code>LatLon</code>](#LatLon) \| [<code>GeoMap</code>](#GeoMap) - The center, or the `GeoMap` when setting.  

| Param | Type |
| --- | --- |
| [lat] | <code>number</code> \| [<code>LatLon</code>](#LatLon) \| <code>Array.&lt;number&gt;</code> | 
| [lon] | <code>number</code> | 

<a name="GeoMap+zoom"></a>

### myMap.zoom([level]) ⇒ <code>number</code> \| <code>GeoMap</code>
Gets or sets the zoom level. Each step doubles the scale; levels match MapLibre
(the whole world is 512 pixels wide at zoom 0).

**Kind**: instance method of [<code>GeoMap</code>](#GeoMap)  
**Returns**: <code>number</code> \| [<code>GeoMap</code>](#GeoMap) - The zoom level (possibly fractional), or the `GeoMap` when setting.  

| Param | Type |
| --- | --- |
| [level] | <code>number</code> | 

<a name="GeoMap+interactive"></a>

### myMap.interactive([enabled]) ⇒ <code>boolean</code> \| <code>GeoMap</code>
Gets or sets whether the map can be dragged and zoomed with the mouse, touch and keyboard.
A locked map can still be moved by code (`center()`, `zoom()`, `flyTo()`, `fit()`), and
dragging on the canvas only reaches the sketch, such as `mouseDragged()`. Use it when the
sketch handles the mouse itself; returning `false` from `mousePressed()` also stops mouse
dragging, with a warning. Has no effect with `basemap: false`.

**Kind**: instance method of [<code>GeoMap</code>](#GeoMap)  
**Returns**: <code>boolean</code> \| [<code>GeoMap</code>](#GeoMap) - Whether the map is interactive, or the `GeoMap` when setting.  

| Param | Type |
| --- | --- |
| [enabled] | <code>boolean</code> | 

**Example**  
```js
// A map that stays put, so dragging draws instead.
myMap = createGeoMap({ center: [35.68, 139.76], zoom: 12, interactive: false });
```
**Example**  
```js
// Press L to lock or unlock the map.
function keyPressed() {
  if (key === 'l') myMap.interactive(!myMap.interactive());
}
```
<a name="GeoMap+fit"></a>

### myMap.fit(data, [options]) ⇒ <code>GeoMap</code>
Centers and zooms so that all of the data is on the canvas.

**Kind**: instance method of [<code>GeoMap</code>](#GeoMap)  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| data | <code>\*</code> |  | Anything [geoPoints](#geoPoints), [geoLines](#geoLines) or [geoPolygons](#geoPolygons)   accept or return, or an array of `{ lat, lon }`. |
| [options] | <code>Object</code> |  |  |
| [options.padding] | <code>number</code> | <code>20</code> | Space to leave around the data, in pixels. |
| [options.maxZoom] | <code>number</code> | <code>16</code> | Upper limit, so a single point isn't zoomed in all the way. |

**Example**  
```js
countries = geoPolygons(await loadJSON('countries.geojson'));
myMap = createGeoMap({ basemap: false });
myMap.fit(countries);
```
<a name="GeoMap+flyTo"></a>

### myMap.flyTo(lat, lon, [zoom]) ⇒ <code>GeoMap</code>
Animates to a place. Without a basemap, jumps there immediately.

**Kind**: instance method of [<code>GeoMap</code>](#GeoMap)  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lat | <code>number</code> |  |
| lon | <code>number</code> |  |
| [zoom] | <code>number</code> | Defaults to the current zoom level. |

<a name="GeoMap+remove"></a>

### myMap.remove()
Removes the map and puts the canvas back where it was. Also happens when the
sketch's `remove()` is called.

**Kind**: instance method of [<code>GeoMap</code>](#GeoMap)  

<a name="geoPoints"></a>

## geoPoints(data, [options]) ⇒ <code>Array.&lt;{lat: number, lon: number, properties: Object}&gt;</code>
Extracts points from a table, an array of objects, or GeoJSON.

- **p5.Table** from `loadTable(file, ',', 'header')`: the latitude and longitude columns are
  found by name (`lat`, `latitude`, `緯度` / `lon`, `lng`, `long`, `longitude`, `経度`, not
  case-sensitive). `properties` holds every column of the row; values that look like numbers
  become numbers, others (such as `"007"`) stay strings. Rows without a valid latitude and
  longitude are skipped, with a warning.
- **Array of objects**: read the same way as table rows.
- **GeoJSON** (FeatureCollection, Feature or geometry): Point and MultiPoint geometries.
  A MultiPoint gives one item per point, sharing `properties`.

**Kind**: global function  
**Throws**:

- <code>Error</code> If no latitude or longitude column is found, or `data` is `undefined`
  (for example, when the file hasn't loaded yet).

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| data | <code>p5.Table</code> \| <code>Array.&lt;Object&gt;</code> \| <code>Object</code> |  |
| [options] | <code>Object</code> |  |
| [options.lat] | <code>string</code> | Name of the latitude column, if it isn't found automatically. |
| [options.lon] | <code>string</code> | Name of the longitude column, if it isn't found automatically. |

**Example**  
```js
const table = await loadTable('places.csv', ',', 'header');
places = geoPoints(table);
// in draw():
for (const place of places) {
  const p = myMap.toScreen(place);
  circle(p.x, p.y, 10);
}
```

<a name="geoLines"></a>

## geoLines(data) ⇒ <code>Array.&lt;{path: Array.&lt;LatLon&gt;, properties: Object}&gt;</code>
Extracts lines from GeoJSON: LineString and MultiLineString geometries.
A MultiLineString gives one item per line, sharing `properties`.

**Kind**: global function  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| data | <code>Object</code> | GeoJSON: a FeatureCollection, a Feature or a geometry. |

**Example**  
```js
for (const line of lines) {
  noFill();
  beginShape();
  for (const p of myMap.toScreen(line.path)) vertex(p.x, p.y);
  endShape();
}
```

<a name="geoPolygons"></a>

## geoPolygons(data) ⇒ <code>Array.&lt;{outer: Array.&lt;LatLon&gt;, holes: Array.&lt;Array.&lt;LatLon&gt;&gt;, properties: Object}&gt;</code>
Extracts polygons from GeoJSON: Polygon and MultiPolygon geometries.
A MultiPolygon gives one item per polygon, sharing `properties`.
`outer` is the outline; `holes` are cut-outs, to draw with `beginContour()` and `endContour()`.

**Kind**: global function  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| data | <code>Object</code> | GeoJSON: a FeatureCollection, a Feature or a geometry. |

**Example**  
```js
beginShape();
for (const p of myMap.toScreen(country.outer)) vertex(p.x, p.y);
for (const hole of country.holes) {
  beginContour();
  for (const p of myMap.toScreen(hole)) vertex(p.x, p.y);
  endContour();
}
endShape(CLOSE);
```

<a name="geo"></a>

## p5.geo
The projection and data helpers as plain functions, independent of p5 and MapLibre.
Available in sketches as `p5.geo`. They are strict: every argument must be a number,
or they throw a `TypeError`.

**Kind**: global namespace  

* [geo](#geo) : <code>object</code>
    * [.TILE_SIZE](#geo.TILE_SIZE) : <code>number</code>
    * [.MAX_LATITUDE](#geo.MAX_LATITUDE) : <code>number</code>
    * [.STYLES](#geo.STYLES) : <code>Object.&lt;string, string&gt;</code>
    * [.VERSION](#geo.VERSION) : <code>string</code>
    * [.containsLatLon(polygon, lat, lon)](#geo.containsLatLon) ⇒ <code>boolean</code>
    * [.geoBounds(data)](#geo.geoBounds) ⇒ <code>Object</code>
    * [.lonToWorldX(lon)](#geo.lonToWorldX) ⇒ <code>number</code>
    * [.latToWorldY(lat)](#geo.latToWorldY) ⇒ <code>number</code>
    * [.worldXToLon(x)](#geo.worldXToLon) ⇒ <code>number</code>
    * [.worldYToLat(y)](#geo.worldYToLat) ⇒ <code>number</code>
    * [.worldSize(zoom)](#geo.worldSize) ⇒ <code>number</code>
    * [.project(lat, lon, view)](#geo.project) ⇒ <code>Object</code>
    * [.projectPath(points, view)](#geo.projectPath) ⇒ <code>Array.&lt;{x: number, y: number}&gt;</code>
    * [.unproject(x, y, view)](#geo.unproject) ⇒ [<code>LatLon</code>](#LatLon)
    * [.fitView(bounds, width, height, [options])](#geo.fitView) ⇒ <code>Object</code>

<a name="geo.TILE_SIZE"></a>

### p5.geo.TILE\_SIZE : <code>number</code>
The width of the world in pixels at zoom 0. MapLibre uses 512, and matching it keeps zoom
levels interchangeable.

**Kind**: static constant of [<code>geo</code>](#geo)  
<a name="geo.MAX_LATITUDE"></a>

### p5.geo.MAX\_LATITUDE : <code>number</code>
The northern and southern limit of Web Mercator, in degrees. Latitudes beyond it are clamped.

**Kind**: static constant of [<code>geo</code>](#geo)  
<a name="geo.STYLES"></a>

### p5.geo.STYLES : <code>Object.&lt;string, string&gt;</code>
The basemap presets for the `basemap` option of [createGeoMap](#createGeoMap): keyless
[OpenFreeMap](https://openfreemap.org/) styles, by name.

**Kind**: static constant of [<code>geo</code>](#geo)  
<a name="geo.VERSION"></a>

### p5.geo.VERSION : <code>string</code>
The version of p5.geo, such as `"0.1.2"`, like `p5.VERSION` for p5.js. Handy for checking
which version a sketch actually loaded, for example when a CDN or browser cache serves an
older one.

**Kind**: static constant of [<code>geo</code>](#geo)  
**Example**  
```js
console.log(p5.geo.VERSION);
```
<a name="geo.containsLatLon"></a>

### p5.geo.containsLatLon(polygon, lat, lon) ⇒ <code>boolean</code>
Whether a latitude and longitude is inside a polygon: inside its outline and outside every
hole. Useful for questions about the data itself, such as which country an earthquake was in.
Edges are treated as straight lines on the map, as they are drawn.

Polygons crossing the antimeridian need to be split there, as GeoJSON recommends.

**Kind**: static method of [<code>geo</code>](#geo)  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| polygon | <code>Object</code> \| [<code>Array.&lt;LatLon&gt;</code>](#LatLon) | An item   from [geoPolygons](#geoPolygons), or an outline as an array of `{ lat, lon }`. |
| lat | <code>number</code> |  |
| lon | <code>number</code> |  |

**Example**  
```js
const inJapan = p5.geo.containsLatLon(japan, quake.lat, quake.lon);
```
<a name="geo.geoBounds"></a>

### p5.geo.geoBounds(data) ⇒ <code>Object</code>
The bounding box of the data.

**Kind**: static method of [<code>geo</code>](#geo)  
**Returns**: <code>Object</code> - `null` if the data is empty.  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| data | <code>\*</code> | Anything [geoPoints](#geoPoints), [geoLines](#geoLines) or [geoPolygons](#geoPolygons) accept   or return, or an array of `{ lat, lon }`. |

<a name="geo.lonToWorldX"></a>

### p5.geo.lonToWorldX(lon) ⇒ <code>number</code>
Longitude → world units (0 at 180°W to 1 at 180°E).

**Kind**: static method of [<code>geo</code>](#geo)  

| Param | Type |
| --- | --- |
| lon | <code>number</code> |

### p5.geo.latToWorldY(lat) ⇒ <code>number</code>
Latitude → world units (0 at the northern limit to 1 at the southern limit).

**Kind**: static method of [<code>geo</code>](#geo)  

| Param | Type |
| --- | --- |
| lat | <code>number</code> | 

<a name="geo.worldXToLon"></a>

### p5.geo.worldXToLon(x) ⇒ <code>number</code>
World units → longitude.

**Kind**: static method of [<code>geo</code>](#geo)  

| Param | Type |
| --- | --- |
| x | <code>number</code> | 

<a name="geo.worldYToLat"></a>

### p5.geo.worldYToLat(y) ⇒ <code>number</code>
World units → latitude.

**Kind**: static method of [<code>geo</code>](#geo)  

| Param | Type |
| --- | --- |
| y | <code>number</code> | 

<a name="geo.worldSize"></a>

### p5.geo.worldSize(zoom) ⇒ <code>number</code>
The width of the world in pixels at a zoom level.

**Kind**: static method of [<code>geo</code>](#geo)  

| Param | Type |
| --- | --- |
| zoom | <code>number</code> | 

<a name="geo.project"></a>

### p5.geo.project(lat, lon, view) ⇒ <code>Object</code>
Latitude/longitude → screen position. Uses the copy of the world nearest the center,
so a point stays visible wherever the map is panned to (the basemap repeats the world sideways).

**Kind**: static method of [<code>geo</code>](#geo)  

| Param | Type |
| --- | --- |
| lat | <code>number</code> | 
| lon | <code>number</code> | 
| view | [<code>View</code>](#View) | 

<a name="geo.projectPath"></a>

### p5.geo.projectPath(points, view) ⇒ <code>Array.&lt;{x: number, y: number}&gt;</code>
Projects a line or polygon outline as one piece: the whole list moves to the copy of the
world nearest the center. Projecting each point separately could tear shapes that straddle
the far side of the world.

**Kind**: static method of [<code>geo</code>](#geo)  

| Param | Type |
| --- | --- |
| points | [<code>Array.&lt;LatLon&gt;</code>](#LatLon) | 
| view | [<code>View</code>](#View) | 

<a name="geo.unproject"></a>

### p5.geo.unproject(x, y, view) ⇒ <code>LatLon</code>
Screen position → latitude/longitude. Longitude is normalized to -180…180.

**Kind**: static method of [<code>geo</code>](#geo)  

| Param | Type |
| --- | --- |
| x | <code>number</code> | 
| y | <code>number</code> | 
| view | [<code>View</code>](#View) | 

<a name="geo.fitView"></a>

### p5.geo.fitView(bounds, width, height, [options]) ⇒ <code>Object</code>
The center and zoom that fit a bounding box on a screen.

**Kind**: static method of [<code>geo</code>](#geo)  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bounds | <code>Object</code> |  |  |
| width | <code>number</code> |  | Screen width in pixels. |
| height | <code>number</code> |  | Screen height in pixels. |
| [options] | <code>Object</code> |  |  |
| [options.padding] | <code>number</code> | <code>20</code> | Space to leave on each side, in pixels. |
| [options.maxZoom] | <code>number</code> | <code>16</code> | Upper limit for the zoom. |

<a name="LatLon"></a>

## LatLon : <code>Object</code>
A latitude and longitude, in degrees.

**Kind**: global typedef  
**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lat | <code>number</code> | Latitude, from -90 (south) to 90 (north). |
| lon | <code>number</code> | Longitude, from -180 (west) to 180 (east). |

<a name="View"></a>

## View : <code>Object</code>
What a map shows: its center sits in the middle of a `width` × `height` screen.

**Kind**: global typedef  
**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lat | <code>number</code> | Latitude of the center. |
| lon | <code>number</code> | Longitude of the center. |
| zoom | <code>number</code> | Zoom level. |
| width | <code>number</code> | Screen width in pixels. |
| height | <code>number</code> | Screen height in pixels. |

## Passing numbers and strings

`GeoMap` methods and the `createGeoMap()` options are forgiving, so that values read from a file can go straight in:

- **Numeric strings become numbers.** `myMap.toScreen('35.6586', '139.7454')` works the same as with numbers, so `table.getString()` results can be passed directly. This applies to `toScreen`, `fromScreen`, `center`, `zoom`, `flyTo`, the `fit` options, and the `center` and `zoom` options of `createGeoMap()`.
- **Other values become `NaN`, with a warning.** An empty string, `null`, `undefined` or text such as `'abc'` gives `NaN` and a console message naming the function and the argument, for example `p5.geo: toScreen() expected a number for lat, but got "abc".` Each function and argument warns only once, so a mistake inside `draw()` doesn't flood the console. Empty values are never treated as `0`.
- **They never throw.**

The functions in `p5.geo` are strict instead: every argument must be a number, or they throw a `TypeError` naming the function and the argument. `NaN` counts as a number and passes through.

For bundlers and TypeScript, see [Using with a bundler](./guide/bundlers.md).
